The Goodwin Model: Behind the Hill Function — Gonze & Abou-Jaoude (2013)
DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0069573; license: CC BY.
Input scope: Results, Limit-cycle Oscillations in the Goodwin Model, including Figure 2 caption.
Parser: deterministic JATS text; formula images remain explicit placeholders.
Task: reconstruct equations (1)-(3) and Figure 2B parameter values. Use the authors' symbol names. Missing initial conditions or inaccessible image content must remain unknown; request researcher input.

Limit-cycle Oscillations in the Goodwin Model The Goodwin model [8], [9] is a simple delayed negative feedback loop model (Fig. 1). Its dynamics is governed by 3 ordinary differential equations: Scheme of the Goodwin model. In the original version of the model, the negative feedback exerted by Z on the synthesis of X is described by a non-linear Hill function. [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.g001] [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e004] [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e005] [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e006] The variables [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e007] , [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e008] and [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e009] can be interpreted as the concentration of a given gene mRNA, the corresponding protein, and a transcriptional inhibitor, respectively. The feedback loop is achieved by the repression exerted by the inhibitor to the mRNA synthesis and is described by a Hill function: [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e010] In 1968, Griffith [9] demonstrated that limit-cycle oscillations can be obtained only if the Hill coefficient [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e011] is larger than 8. For [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e012] , the model displays damped oscillations. The Hill function and the limit-cycle oscillations obtained by numerical integration of the Goodwin model are shown in Fig. 2. For the parameter values chosen ( [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e013] ), [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e014] remains always above the threshold [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e015] and the oscillations are rather sinusoidal. When [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e016] increases, we can make [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e017] switching around [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.e018] , inducing relaxation oscillations [13]. [IMAGE_FORMULA: info:doi/10.1371/journal.pone.0069573.g002] In the following, our primary goal is to replace the Hill function in Eq. (1) by a realistic molecular mechanism, namely a multisite phosphorylation process, and to show that the Hill function is a proper description of the kinetics of this mechanistic model, at least under some conditions.
